opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, write is within the allowed maximum (admin would require owning the Payroll Specialist role, which this employee does not hold). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E007 is a contractor with basic security training (note that this conflicts with the earlier note claiming full-time). As a contractor with basic training, max access is read; requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR note (authoritative for employment status) states E007 is a full-time Analyst. As a full-time employee, the maximum allowed access to Payroll is write (admin would require owning the Payroll Specialist role, which an Analyst does not). The requested level is write, which is at the maximum, so grant write.

- Note 2 (from Security?): role Analyst (not looked up; same value as note 1), employment type contractor (looked up in own database), security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says contractor with basic training, max access is read.

Conflict: full_time vs contractor. The HR note says full_time, security note says contractor.

The two notes conflict on employment type. Note 1 says full_time; note 2 says contractor with basic security training, max read.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time: requested write <= max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → grant read.

The security note says "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" for role, but for employment type it says "looked up in own database before writing" and says contractor. So security looked up employment type and found contractor, basic training, recommending read.

HR note says full_time (looked up in own database). Conflict.
